perspective:
From Mason Hurley’s available perspective:

- Mason is an accountant at a small community center and works with Martha Moua, a personal care aide there. Their relationship is professional and work-related, not personally close.
- While reviewing financial reports, Mason noticed discrepancies: healthcare expenses seemed unusually high and did not match usual spending patterns. This made him suspicious and anxious, and he initially believed Martha might be mismanaging funds.
- Mason spoke with Martha about the report. He told her the numbers didn’t add up and pointed to the healthcare expenses. Martha said there was likely a reasonable explanation, looked at the issue, said it might be a misentry, and promised to review and correct any errors.
- After reviewing the report with Martha, Mason accepted that the discrepancies were a simple clerical error, not mismanagement. He felt relieved and embarrassed about his initial suspicion.
- Mason apologized to Martha for suspecting her. Martha said it was okay, that errors happen, that she understood he was being thorough, and suggested double-checking entries next time.
- Mason came to believe Martha was competent but that the current financial management system was inadequate. He felt frustrated with the system and empathetic toward Martha.
- Mason proposed creating a new, more robust financial system. Martha agreed, said it was a great idea, and offered to help. Mason said he would draft a proposal and wanted her input.
- Mason drafted the proposal. He believed it would benefit operations but was uncertain whether management would approve or implement it. Martha told him it was solid, encouraged him to present it confidently, and agreed to help gather data.
- Mason prepared and presented the proposal to management. He thought the presentation went well, felt satisfied but exhausted, and believed he had done everything he could. He understood the decision was now up to management.
- Martha praised his work and suggested he take time off. Mason thanked her, said he would take a few days off to recharge and reflect, and hoped for good news. Martha wished him a good break and offered help while he was away.
- Mason does not yet know management’s decision and does not have access to Martha’s private thoughts beyond what she said or did in their interactions.
